text:
jess-support: Hey folks — customer acme-inc reported a surge of 5xx responses from our hosted inference API this morning. They say requests to the token refresh path (/v1/auth/refresh) started returning 502/503 instead of 429. Escalating, link to convo in ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/ACME-423 :rotating_light:

mike-sre: ack. can you paste a sample request/response + request_id and trace_id? any timeline (when it started, p95 latency)?

jess-support: repro snippet from customer:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/auth/refresh \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <refresh>' \
  -d '{"client_id":"acme","scope":"infer"}'
```
response headers:
```
HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
Content-Type: application/json
X-Request-ID: req_202403060930_abc123
X-Trace-ID: trace-0a1b2c
```
logs they forwarded:
```
quota-orch: upstream timeout to auth-svc (deadline exceeded) for tenant acme, returned 502
rate-limiter: fallback path attempted, returned opaque 502 instead of 429
```
Happened at 2024-03-06T09:30:12Z, lasted ~8m, then trended back.

sara-eng: thanks. initial hunch: quota-orch is timing out to our auth/token service and currently the fallback is the degenerate path that returns 5xx. we should be returning 4xx for client quota errors. can we verify classifier output? @mike-sre any immediate mitigations?

mike-sre: checking metrics now. I see a spike in quota-orch latency p99 -> 12s for that time window. auth-svc p95 also increased. looks like connection pool exhaustion on auth-svc side.

tony-ops: I'm seeing a correlated spike in egress latency to auth-svc region us-west-2; autoscaling didn't kick due to a bug in the scale policy (min replicas pinned). scaling it up now. will also increase auth-svc pool temporarily.

jess-support: customer impacted: multiple API keys returning 502, they want repro steps and ETA.

mike-sre: request_id req_202403060930_abc123 and trace trace-0a1b2c match logs. capture shows quota-orch attempted to contact auth-svc and hit deadline 3s -> bubbled up. classifier set to FALLTHROUGH_ON_TIMEOUT=true which currently maps to 5xx. that's wrong for client token issues.

sara-eng: can we hotfix mapping to return 429 when the auth service indicates a client quota deny or token invalid, and only 5xx for infra errors? quick patch: change fallback mapping in quota-orch/router: ``FALLBACK_HTTP_STATUS = is_client_error ? 429 : 502``. roll it behind feature flag.

mike-sre: deploying a canary of that change to staging now. deploy-bot: deploy start sha=ab12cd

deploy-bot: deploy complete canary env sha=ab12cd :rocket:

mike-sre: canary looks good for token-refresh route (no 5xx on simulated auth timeouts). promoting to prod in ~5m.

tony-ops: scaling changes applied to auth-svc. monitoring egress latency.

jess-support: told customer we'll roll out a fix and follow up with postmortem. they asked for a workaround in the meantime — any suggestions?

sara-eng: workaround: retry with exponential backoff and check for 5xx vs 4xx. but note we should fix server side mapping asap. also add temporary circuit-breaker to reduce retry storm.

mike-sre: prod rollout done; initial metrics show 5xx on token-refresh dropped to baseline and replaced by 429 where appropriate. capturing a few sample responses for the ticket.

jess-support: thanks — passing to customer with ETA + CC support manager. we'll follow up with a short postmortem once metrics stabilize. :white_check_mark:

sara-eng: filing follow-up issue to remove FALLTHROUGH_ON_TIMEOUT flag and improve classifier tests. putting link in ticket.

mike-sre: adding monitoring alert: quota-orch upstream timeout > 1s -> page. also creating dashboard for token-refresh 4xx/5xx ratio.

deploy-bot: incident resolved marker created: INCIDENT-ACME-20240306
